accepted.s: Which one of the following officials was the head of the army department in the Delhi Sultanate?
accepted.x: The Ariz-i-Mamalik was the head of the army department.
accepted.tq: Match the official with the precise department under his charge.
accepted.sec: Officials → duty  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Sadr-us-Sudur in the Delhi Sultanate was primarily associated with which of the following functions?
accepted.x: The Sadr-us-Sudur supervised religious affairs and endowments; the Chief Sadr was also the Chief Qazi.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between officials whose functions belonged to religion, intelligence and court administration.
accepted.sec: Officials → duty  [other exams]

accepted.s:
With reference to the central officials of the Delhi Sultanate, consider the following statements:
1. Qazi-ul-Quzat was the Chief Justice.
2. Barid-i-Mumalik headed the news and intelligence system.
3. Wakil-i-Dar was responsible for court decorum and the royal household.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Qazi-ul-Quzat was the Chief Justice, Barid-i-Mumalik headed intelligence, and Wakil-i-Dar supervised the court and royal household.
accepted.tq: Use the official-function pairings and check all three statements independently.
accepted.sec: Officials → duty  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Barid-i-Mumalik — Head of news and intelligence
accepted.x: Wakil-i-Dar was responsible for court decorum and the royal household. The Chief Justice was the Qazi-ul-Quzat.
accepted.tq: Find the official whose duty has been swapped with that of another official.
accepted.sec: Officials → duty  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between sharia and zawabit in the Delhi Sultanate?
o: Zawabit replaced sharia in all civil and criminal matters.
Sharia governed all criminal matters, while zawabit governed only Hindu personal law.
Sharia applied only to the Sultan and his nobles, whereas zawabit applied to the general population.
Sharia covered Muslims’ civil matters, while royal decrees called zawabit supplemented it.
accepted.x: Sharia covered the civil matters of Muslims, while royal decrees or zawabit supplemented the legal order. Criminal law followed the Sultan’s rules, and Hindus retained their personal law.
accepted.tq: Separate civil law, personal law, criminal rules and royal decrees rather than treating them as one system.
accepted.sec: Legal basis and nature of the state - sharia vs zawabit, composite elements  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the legal and administrative nature of the Delhi Sultanate:
1. Hindus generally retained their own personal law.
2. Criminal law followed the rules made by the Sultans.
3. The Sultan was the supreme commander and the highest court of appeal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Hindu personal law was retained, criminal law was governed by the Sultan’s rules, and the Sultan combined supreme military and appellate authority.
accepted.tq: Test the institutional features separately and select the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Legal basis and nature of the state - sharia vs zawabit, composite elements  [other exams]

accepted.s: The state under the Delhi Sultanate was described as a composite structure because it combined which of the following elements?
accepted.x: The Delhi Sultanate combined Perso-Arabic, Turko-Mongol and Indian elements and was comparatively centralised.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact three-part composition instead of substituting neighbouring cultural influences.
accepted.sec: Legal basis and nature of the state - sharia vs zawabit, composite elements  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following was a Perso-Arabic element in the political culture of the Delhi Sultanate?
1. The title Sultan
2. The Caliph’s nominal authority
3. Persian court rituals such as sijda, paibos and Nauroz
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The title Sultan, the nominal authority of the Caliph and Persian court rituals such as sijda, paibos and Nauroz were Perso-Arabic elements.
accepted.tq: Group the cultural features under their stated civilisational component.
accepted.sec: Legal basis and nature of the state - sharia vs zawabit, composite elements  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the Turko-Mongol influence on the Delhi Sultanate?
o: An army organised in decimal units and based on mounted archers
A hereditary bureaucracy organised around village assemblies
An army based mainly on war elephants and naval forces
A revenue system based exclusively on temple endowments
accepted.x: The Turko-Mongol elements included decimal military organisation and power based on horse warfare with mounted archers.
accepted.tq: Link the military structure and method of warfare to the correct cultural influence.
accepted.sec: Legal basis and nature of the state - sharia vs zawabit, composite elements  [other exams]

accepted.s: The intelligence network of the comparatively centralised Delhi Sultanate primarily consisted of which officials?
accepted.x: Barids functioned as the intelligence network of the centralised Sultanate state.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution by its specialised function rather than its administrative level.
accepted.sec: Legal basis and nature of the state - sharia vs zawabit, composite elements  [other exams]

accepted.s: What was the principal characteristic of the nobility during the Slave dynasty?
o: It was open equally to all Indian communities.
It was dominated by Afghan tribal chiefs.
It consisted mainly of hereditary Hindu zamindars.
accepted.x: The nobility under the Slave dynasty was characterised by a Turkish monopoly.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the ethnic composition of the nobility under different dynasties.
accepted.sec: Nobility - ethnic composition, the Chalisa  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Turkan-i-Chahalgani:
1. It was created by Iltutmish.
2. It consisted of forty Turkish slave-nobles.
3. Balban ultimately destroyed its political influence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Iltutmish created the Turkan-i-Chahalgani, or the Forty, of Turkish slave-nobles. They influenced the succession after him, but Balban destroyed their power.
accepted.tq: Check the institution through its founder, composition and later fate.
accepted.sec: Nobility - ethnic composition, the Chalisa  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which development is associated with the Khalji Revolution of 1290?
o: The Sultan was reduced to a ceremonial position.
All nobles were made hereditary landholders.
High offices were opened to non-Turks and Indian Muslims.
High offices were restricted to Turkish slave-nobles.
accepted.x: The Khalji Revolution opened high office to non-Turks and Indian Muslims, breaking the earlier Turkish monopoly.
accepted.tq: Use the date and institutional change together to identify the correct development.
accepted.sec: Nobility - ethnic composition, the Chalisa  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with the policy concerning nobility?
o: Muhammad bin Tughluq — Promoted foreigners and low-born men
Alauddin Khalji — Crushed the Balbani and Jalali nobles
Lodi Sultans — Treated Afghan nobles as subordinate officials without tribal equality
accepted.x: Lodi rulers dealt with an Afghan tribal nobility that treated the Sultan as first among equals. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Detect the reversed description in a dynasty-wise comparison of nobility.
accepted.sec: Nobility - ethnic composition, the Chalisa  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Iltutmish created the Turkan-i-Chahalgani.
B. Jalaluddin Khalji came to power.
C. Alauddin Khalji banned noble gatherings and spied on the nobility.
D. Balban destroyed the power of the Forty.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Iltutmish created the Forty, Balban destroyed its power, Jalaluddin Khalji came to power in 1290, and Alauddin later imposed restrictions on the nobility.
accepted.tq: Fix the founder and the later destroyer first, then place the Khalji developments.
accepted.sec: Nobility - ethnic composition, the Chalisa  [other exams]

accepted.s: An iqta in the Delhi Sultanate was primarily a:
o: Religious endowment administered by the Chief Sadr
Village-level account maintained by the Patwari
Permanent ownership grant of agricultural land
Assignment of land revenue in place of a cash salary
accepted.x: An iqta was an assignment of land revenue in place of cash salary; it did not confer ownership of the land.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a revenue assignment from ownership of land.
accepted.sec: Iqta system - origin, muqti, transferability, fawazil, comparisons  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the functions of a muqti or iqtadar?
o: He collected revenue, maintained troops and kept order in the assigned territory.
He served exclusively as the Sultan’s chief judge.
He acted only as a village accountant and maintained crop records.
He supervised only religious endowments and charitable grants.
accepted.x: The muqti or iqtadar collected revenue, maintained troops and preserved order in the iqta.
accepted.tq: Match the holder of the assignment with the complete set of operational duties.
accepted.sec: Iqta system - origin, muqti, transferability, fawazil, comparisons  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the development of the iqta system is correct?
o: Firoz Tughluq abolished the iqta system completely.
Iltutmish built the iqta into a systematic administrative institution.
Alauddin Khalji converted every iqta into private property.
Qutbuddin Aibak first introduced it as a hereditary system in India.
accepted.x: Iltutmish developed the iqta into a system. Under the Sultanate, it remained a revenue assignment rather than private ownership.
accepted.tq: Identify the ruler associated with institutional consolidation, not later modification.
accepted.sec: Iqta system - origin, muqti, transferability, fawazil, comparisons  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under which ruler did iqtas become hereditary?
accepted.x: Iqtas became hereditary under Firoz Tughluq, strengthening the position of the nobles.
accepted.tq: Use the succession of transferable and hereditary arrangements to isolate the later change.
accepted.sec: Iqta system - origin, muqti, transferability, fawazil, comparisons  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: What did the term ‘fawazil’ signify in the iqta system?
o: The hereditary right of the muqti over the land
The military contingent permanently stationed at the capital
The surplus revenue remaining after the muqti’s costs, which was sent to the treasury
The tax imposed on village artisans
accepted.x: Fawazil was the surplus revenue left after meeting the muqti’s costs, and it had to be remitted to the treasury.
accepted.tq: Distinguish surplus revenue from the assignment, officer and military obligations of an iqta.
accepted.sec: Iqta system - origin, muqti, transferability, fawazil, comparisons  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following systems was associated with the Vijayanagara Empire?
accepted.x: Amaram or nayankara was the Vijayanagara system in which land was granted to amaranayakas for maintaining troops.
accepted.tq: Identify the system by pairing it with the correct empire and military obligation.
accepted.sec: Iqta system - origin, muqti, transferability, fawazil, comparisons  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Iqta — Delhi Sultanate
2. Jagir — Mughal Empire
3. Amaram — Vijayanagara Empire
4. Mokasa — Bahmani and later Deccan
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Iqta, jagir, amaram and mokasa belonged respectively to the Delhi Sultanate, Mughal Empire, Vijayanagara and Bahmani-later Deccan contexts.
accepted.tq: Compare the four revenue assignments by both region and administrative nature.
accepted.sec: Iqta system - origin, muqti, transferability, fawazil, comparisons  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Mahrousa meant a protected town. Khalisa referred to land under state administration, shiq to a portion or division, and iqta to a revenue assignment.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure terminological pair and eliminate the swapped meanings.
accepted.sec: Iqta system - origin, muqti, transferability, fawazil, comparisons  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A district-level officer in the Delhi Sultanate responsible for a shiq was known as the:
accepted.x: The Shiqdar was in charge of a shiq, or district.
accepted.tq: Match the official to the exact territorial unit under his charge.
accepted.sec: Local and revenue officials → role  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Muqti or wali — Governor of an iqta
Amil — Revenue officer of a pargana
accepted.x: A Khut was a hereditary rural landholder. The despatcher of royal decrees was the Khareetadar.
accepted.tq: Identify the official whose role has been replaced by a central court function.
accepted.sec: Local and revenue officials → role  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
With reference to rural officials of the Delhi Sultanate, consider the following statements:
1. Muqaddam or Chaudhari was the village headman.
2. The Chaudhari was regarded as the chief rural land-revenue official.
3. Alauddin Khalji abolished the cess of the khut.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The muqaddam or chaudhari headed the village, the chaudhari had a major rural revenue role, and Alauddin abolished the khut’s cess.
accepted.tq: Combine the village hierarchy with the specific revenue measure associated with Alauddin.
accepted.sec: Local and revenue officials → role  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the responsibilities of the Ariz-i-Mamalik?
o: Administering religious endowments and civil law
Recruiting, inspecting and paying the army
Collecting revenue from every village personally
Maintaining the Sultan’s private correspondence only
accepted.x: The Ariz-i-Mamalik recruited, inspected and paid the army.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete military-administrative responsibility.
accepted.sec: Military - ariz-i-mamalik and army structure  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The army of the Delhi Sultanate was characterised by which of the following?
o: A militia composed exclusively of village headmen
An infantry-only force supported by naval units
A cavalry-heavy force supported by infantry, archers and elephants
accepted.x: The army was cavalry-heavy and also included infantry, archers and elephants.
accepted.tq: Identify the dominant arm while retaining the supporting components.
accepted.sec: Military - ariz-i-mamalik and army structure  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which ruler is associated with the creation of the first standing army paid in cash, along with the systems of dagh and huliya?
accepted.x: Alauddin Khalji created the first standing army paid in cash and introduced dagh and huliya in military administration.
accepted.tq: Link the military reform, payment method and identifying administrative terms to one ruler.
accepted.sec: Military - ariz-i-mamalik and army structure  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements best expresses the significance of the Delhi Sultanate’s administrative institutions for the Mughal Empire?
o: The Sultanate diwans anticipated institutions such as the Mughal Diwan, Mir Bakshi and Sadr-us-Sudur.
The Sultanate had no specialised departments that could influence later administrations.
Only the Sultanate’s village institutions survived in the Mughal system.
The Mughal Empire rejected all Sultanate administrative institutions.
accepted.x: The Sultanate diwans prefigured important Mughal institutions, including the Diwan, Mir Bakshi and Sadr-us-Sudur.
accepted.tq: Recognise institutional continuity across two successive imperial systems.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: In the administration of the Qutb Shahi kingdom, which official was associated with finance?
accepted.x: Mir Jumla was the finance official in the Qutb Shahi administration.
accepted.tq: Match each Qutb Shahi office with its specialised portfolio.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Qutb Shahi administration:
1. The Peshwa functioned as the Prime Minister.
2. Under Tana Shah, the title Peshwa was renamed Diwan.
3. Madanna was the last holder of the Peshwa office.
4. Majumdar was an auditor and was mostly drawn from Hindus.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Peshwa was the Prime Minister, was renamed Diwan under Tana Shah, was last held by Madanna, and the Majumdar served as auditor, mostly from the Hindu community.
accepted.tq: Check the office, renaming, last holder and community detail separately.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched in the Qutb Shahi administration?
accepted.x: Mir Jumla was associated with finance. The master of ceremonies in the Delhi Sultanate was the Amir-i-Hajib.
accepted.tq: Detect the office transferred from the Delhi Sultanate to the wrong Qutb Shahi official.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Prime Minister of the Bahmani state was known as the:
accepted.x: The Bahmani Prime Minister was known as the Wakil-us-Saltanat.
accepted.tq: Separate the Bahmani title from the similarly placed Qutb Shahi offices.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between the Bahmani and Qutb Shahi administrative systems and the Delhi Sultanate?
o: Only the Qutb Shahis borrowed from the Delhi model; the Bahmanis did not.
The Delhi model was adopted only in village administration and not at the central level.
Both inherited elements of the Delhi administrative model.
Both rejected the offices of finance, military administration and correspondence.
accepted.x: The Bahmani state and the Qutb Shahis inherited the Delhi model, including institutions such as Wakil-us-Saltanat, Amir-i-Jumla, Peshwa, Mir Jumla and Diwan-i-Insha.
accepted.tq: Test institutional inheritance by comparing the two successor states with the Delhi model.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: After 1323, Andhra was administered from Devagiri under which official, while Malik Maqbul was associated with Warangal?
accepted.x: After 1323, Andhra was administered from Devagiri under Malik Burhanuddin, while Malik Maqbul was associated with Warangal.
accepted.tq: Keep the two officials linked to their respective administrative centres.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
